The Advocate General
Each state has an Advocate-General, an official corresponding to the
Attorney-General of India and having similar functions for the State:
He is appointed by the Governor of the state and holds office during
the pleasure of the Governor:
Only a person who is qualified to be a judge of a High Court can be
appointed Advocate-General: He receives such remuneration as the
Governor may determine:
He has the right to speak and to take part in the proceedings of, but no
right to vote in, the Houses of the Legislature of the state {Ref: Art
177}.
